scene.bubble: What will work look like? Learn will, going to and the present continuous to talk about the future.
scene.intro: For the last part of the Inspiring Nordic project, we asked a big question: what will work look like in the future? In this unit you read what a robotics engineer told our class, you learn the different future forms — will, going to and the present continuous — and you talk about your own plans and predictions. Nobody knows exactly what the future will bring, but if you learn a real skill, the future will need you.

data.title: What will work look like?
data.author: sofia
data.text:
For the last part of our Inspiring Nordic project, we asked a big question: what will work look like in the future? We interviewed teachers, parents and even a robotics engineer.

Some things are going to change a lot. Robots are already building cars, and soon they will do many simple jobs. Our engineer said, “Machines are getting cleverer every year.” But she also told us not to worry. “Machines will never replace real skills,” she explained. “A robot can cut wood, but it can't design a beautiful chair or comfort a frightened patient.”

In the future, many students in this class are going to have jobs that don't exist yet. That sounds a little scary, but it is also exciting. The most important thing, everyone agreed, is to keep learning.

Interestingly, some very old trades are coming back. People want real, handmade things again — furniture, bread, clothes made with care. Even in The Hunchback of Notre Dame, the craftsmen who built the cathedral are still remembered today.

So what are you going to be? Nobody knows for sure. But if you learn a real skill and never stop being curious, the future will need you.

data.title: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous
data.intro: At B1 we choose between three ways to talk about the future, depending on the meaning.

examples.text: We're meeting the engineer on Friday.

rules: will for predictions and quick decisions: It will rain. I'll help you.
going to for plans and intentions you already have: I'm going to be a designer.
present continuous for fixed arrangements with a time: We're visiting the lab at 10.

activities.title: Listening — a visit from an engineer. Write ONE word in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voz: la profesora (Miss Vega), presentando a la ingeniera.
data.script: Good morning, Grade 8. Today we welcome a robotics engineer, Ms Torres. She's going to talk about the future of work. She says that robots will do many simple jobs, but they will never replace human creativity. In ten years, she thinks, most of you will work in teams with machines. Her advice is simple: learn a real skill and keep your curiosity. After the talk, we're visiting the robotics lab at eleven o'clock. Bring your questions!

activities.title: Speaking — talk about the future. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: In pairs, talk about the future using will, going to and the present continuous. Model: “What are you going to do after school?” — “I'm going to study design. I think it'll be useful.” 1) What are you going to do next weekend? 2) What job do you think you'll have one day? 3) How will technology change our school? 4) What are you doing this evening? Then record your best answers.

homework.prompt: Write a short paragraph (6–8 sentences) about your future for the Inspiring Nordic project, using future forms. Say what you are going to study, what job you think you will have, and one prediction about the future of work. Use will, going to and the present continuous. Capital letters and full stops!
